_comment: Opponent archetypes. Shares from limitlesstcg.com/decks (Standard, August 2026). `confidence: high` means the attacker is modelled card-exact; `medium` means the archetype is approximated from its role and results.
_bench: Each archetype's Active is one statistical Pokemon; `bench` is the softest target worth gusting to, which is what Boss's Orders, Prime Catcher and Lisia's Appeal act on. Evolution decks sit on 60-70 HP one-prize basics (Dreepy, Applin, Abra) and are cheap to punish; Basic-attacker decks bench other chunky bodies, so their number is much higher and gusting them is usually not worth a card. This is the whole reason gust cards are worth different amounts against different decks, and modelling it as a single number per archetype is an approximation, not a claim about any specific list.

decks.name: Dragapult ex
decks.note: Card-exact: 320 HP Stage 2, Phantom Dive [R][P] 200 plus 6 damage counters spread, no Weakness, Tera prevents damage while Benched. Reference list runs 4 Crushing Hammer, 2 Team Rocket's Watchtower, 4 Lillie's Determination.

decks.name: N's Zoroark ex
decks.note: Card-exact: 280 HP Darkness Stage 1, Night Joker copies a Benched N's Pokémon attack. Being a Darkness Pokémon it cannot be Confused by Dark Bell, so the Abyss Eye auto-KO line does not function in this matchup.

decks.name: Crustle Rock Inn
decks.note: Single-prize engine deck. Modelled as a fast, low-HP, 1-prize attacker — the worst prize-trade shape to face with 3-prize Megas.

decks.name: Slowking Inspiration
decks.note: Single-prize control. Moderate damage plus light resource denial.

decks.name: Hydrapple ex
decks.note: Grass attacker. Both Megas are Grass-Weak, so its damage is doubled against them.

decks.name: Alakazam Powerful Hand
decks.note: Single-prize Psychic attacker scaling off hand size.

decks.name: Raging Bolt ex
decks.note: Big Dragon Basic. High damage, no Weakness interaction either way.
